verdict.root_cause: An automated environment update at 06:29:24Z set REDIS_ADDR on cartservice to a redis-cart endpoint on non-default port 6380, where no override existed before [tr_fab2d19614fa]. cartservice cannot reach Redis at that address: every start attempts the connection, fails, and throws an unhandled ApplicationException out of RedisCartStore initialization in Program Main, producing a sustained crash-restart loop with at least six cycles between 06:31:57 and 06:33:40 and no request-handling lines at all [tr_5c4e8003546e]. Because the process never reaches a serving state, checkoutservice's client call to CartService/GetCart fails immediately — under 1.5ms, no server-side cartservice span — aborting PlaceOrder before payment, currency, shipping or email, and propagating up through frontend [tr_50185e505dae, tr_6d291b909357]. checkoutservice has no change record and is relaying, not originating, the failure [tr_a789ea138e79].
verdict.reasoning: The REDIS_ADDR override is the only change in the minutes before onset; the nearest image change was a revert ~31 minutes prior and the latency-injection container was removed ~11 minutes prior, so neither a bad artifact nor an active delay fault was in place [tr_fab2d19614fa]. The port logged in each failing connection attempt matches the changed value, and the failure is at startup initialization rather than request handling [tr_5c4e8003546e]. The caller-side signature — uniform abort at GetCart, sub-millisecond, no server span — is that of an absent callee, not a slow or erroring one, which excludes dependency_latency [tr_50185e505dae]. No artifact change makes bad_deploy unsupported; nothing points to a limit being hit. The wrong address is itself the mechanism, so reverting the value, not restarting, is the fix.
open_questions: Nobody queried redis-cart directly; whether anything listens on 6380 is unconfirmed, and the 10-30s time-to-failure reads as timeout rather than refusal [tr_5c4e8003546e].
Crash-loop onset is not pinned — logs are truncated between 06:02:05 and 06:31:57, so the transition relative to the 06:29:24 change was not observed [tr_5c4e8003546e].

checkoutservice's error ratio was ~59% in the 05:30-06:02 baseline and fell to ~6-7% across the alert window [tr_4b559a3405b5], indicating an earlier, unexplained disturbance this change does not account for.

alternatives.root_cause: The redis-cart backend is itself down or unreachable, and cartservice would crash-loop regardless of the configured port.
alternatives.why_not: Not excluded, since no dispatch touched redis-cart — but the config edit landed two minutes before onset and named exactly the address in the failing connection lines [tr_fab2d19614fa, tr_5c4e8003546e], which fits better than an independent backend failure coinciding to the minute.

alternatives.root_cause: The 06:32 alert is the tail of an earlier cartservice disturbance driven by the repeated automated fault-injection cycle, not a fresh onset.
alternatives.why_not: It may explain the pre-06:02 elevated errors [tr_4b559a3405b5], but the crash loop observed at window end has a concrete active mechanism tied to the current REDIS_ADDR value [tr_5c4e8003546e], so it does not displace the primary cause for the ongoing failure.

proposal.expected_effect: Restoring cartservice's prior environment (no REDIS_ADDR override, i.e. the default redis-cart endpoint rather than :6380) and recreating the container should let RedisCartStore initialization complete. Observable as: (1) in Loki {service="cart-service"}, the repeating 'connection attempt -> failure -> unhandled ApplicationException from RedisCartStore init in Program Main' cycle stops appearing, and GetCartAsync/AddItemAsync request-handling lines resume at roughly the pre-incident rate seen at 06:02; (2) in Jaeger, failing PlaceOrder traces stop terminating at the checkoutservice client span for CartService/GetCart, and a server-side cartservice GetCart span reappears in traces; (3) frontend/checkoutservice PlaceOrder traces complete the full downstream chain (currency, payment, shipping, email, orders publish) again. Note the ~6-7% checkoutservice error ratio [tr_4b559a3405b5] is NOT predicted to change, since that disturbance predates this change and is unexplained.
proposal.if_wrong: Falsified if, after the recreate, cart-service logs still show the same connect-fail-ApplicationException cycle at the reverted address — that would mean redis-cart is itself unreachable/down and the port was incidental. Nobody queried redis-cart directly, so it is unconfirmed that anything listens on either port; the 10-30s time-to-failure per attempt reads as timeout rather than refusal [tr_5c4e8003546e], which is weakly consistent with the host, not just the port, being wrong. Also falsified if cartservice comes up cleanly but checkoutservice GetCart spans keep erroring — that would put the break on the checkoutservice->cartservice edge rather than in cart's Redis config. Partial-failure risk: the change log shows platform-automation applying and reverting this same override on a cycle [tr_fab2d19614fa], so a revert may be re-applied by automation within minutes; a recovery that flaps back into crash-loop is not a success.
proposal.risk: If the 6380 endpoint was a deliberate migration target rather than a fault, reverting points cartservice at a stale or decommissioned Redis: carts read from the wrong store, users see emptied or divergent carts, and the outage continues under a different cause. The recreate itself drops the process and any in-process cache, so every in-flight GetCart/AddItem fails during restart. And because the change actor is automation on a repeating cycle, a manual revert may fight the automation and produce restart flapping — worse than a steady crash-loop for anyone doing capacity or alert work. This does not address the pre-06:02 disturbance behind the ~59% baseline error ratio, so declaring the incident closed on this alone would be wrong.
proposal.blast_radius: cartservice only, for the duration of the recreate. Its inbound caller in this incident is checkoutservice (and frontend transitively, and loadgenerator's traffic through frontend) — they see connection resets while the container comes back, on top of the failures they already see. Because the reverted value is a dependency address, the redis-cart endpoints see traffic move: the :6380 target stops receiving connection attempts and the default-port target starts receiving them.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Critical alerts hitting checkout and frontend simultaneously with user-facing impact cannot be dismissed, and no open incident could absorb them. Simultaneous onset across the checkout path suggests a shared dependency or deploy, but nothing in the alerts distinguishes them yet.
